items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

ctx.x: So you start to get established, and what was the Lionel Hampton gig like for you?

Very interesting. What happened, I got to New York and as I was telling a couple of students today, they wanted to know how did I motivate myself and get ahead. I said go to all the jam sessions. Even if it’s not a jam session, if you go to hear somebody play and you feel you’re sure you can play, try to do that. So Lionel Hampton was working at a place called the Metropole Lounge, on Seventh Avenue around 47, 48th street. And he wasn’t using a piano player. You know he was using guitar. Bill Maker was playing…
